spans.s: kuśa, cf. kuśa-kkāṇam (SITI), Tamil, tax on the potters.
kuśala (IA 17), used in the sense of puṇya, religious merit; cf. kuśala-mūla.
kuśala-mūla (CII 2-1; ML), ‘the root of merit’; used to indicate ‘a pious deed’.

Kuśalin (CII 3; SII 3; IA 9), ‘being in good health’, used in the preamble of charters to indicate the genuineness and validity of the grant made by the donors when they were in a healthy state of body and mind; epithet of a donor of copper-plate grants to indicate that the charters were issued when the donor was not subject to any disease like madness.
kuśa-latā-pūta-hast-odakena , cf. udaka-pūrvam, etc. See Ind. Ep., p. 395
kuśa-kkāṇam (SITI), Tamil; tax on potters; also known as tirigaiāyam, śakkara-kkāṇikkai.
